candidates.statement: 1. Let f ∈zCn[[z]] be a formal solution to the diﬀerence equation f(pz) = G(f(z)) Then f converges to an analytic function in some neighborhood of zero.
candidates.proof_excerpt: Let f(z) = P n≥1 fnzn, and G(y) = P n≥1 gnyn, where gn are multilinear operators. Since G is analytic at zero, there exists A > 0 such that the norms of the coeﬃcients are estimated by |gn| < An for all n. Let k0 be so big that for k ≥k0 one has|(pk −g1)−1| < 2|p|−k, and 2A < |p|
